# GitHub Copilot & Codex Instructions

- Code coverage must stay at or above 90% per-file for statements, branches, functions, and lines.
- Always generate unit tests for new or edited functions, components, routes, and controllers.
- Ensure all tests complete within the 10000ms global timeout.
- Run `npm run test:coverage` to confirm all coverage thresholds are satisfied.
- Always use the centralized structured logger (`backend/src/utils/logger.ts` or `frontend/src/utils/logger.ts`). No raw `console.log`/`console.error`.
- In local mode, persist logs to `logs/` on the file system and ensure automatic purging of expired logs for compliance.
- Include structured context (timestamp, level, service, message, context, requestId, durationMs, error details) in all log calls.
- PR CI/CD workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` validates linting, typechecking, building, and 90% per-file code coverage.
- All CI/CD jobs must have an explicit timeout (`timeout-minutes: 15`).
- The CI/CD workflow must post and update an executive summary PR comment detailing test success/failure counts and coverage metrics.
- Maintain a workspace file `prompts.md` storing ONLY user-provided prompts. Never save AI-generated conversations or responses in `prompts.md`.
- Move all user-facing literal strings into constants and access via `UI_STRINGS` (`frontend/src/constants/uiStrings.ts`). No hardcoded UI strings.
- Use template placeholders for dynamic substitution and assert against `UI_STRINGS` constants in all unit tests.
- All constants (defaults, rates, thresholds, palettes, lookups) must reside in dedicated constants files under `constants/` (`frontend/src/constants/` and `backend/src/constants/`). No inline constants or magic numbers.
- All TypeScript types, interfaces, enums, and component prop definitions must reside in dedicated files under `types/` (`frontend/src/types/` and `backend/src/types/`). No inline `interface` or `type` declarations in components, services, or controllers.
- All user and system inputs (frontend forms, modals, API routes, controller bodies, query parameters, headers) must be strictly validated using schemas in `constants/validation.ts` and inferred types in `types/validation.ts`. No inline validation schemas.
- Always implement user-facing error messages with actionable context and specific failure details across categories (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, `AUTH_ERROR`, `NOT_FOUND_ERROR`, `CONFLICT_ERROR`, `SERVER_ERROR`, `RATE_LIMIT_ERROR`). Centralize all error text in `UI_STRINGS` (`frontend/src/constants/uiStrings.ts`), keep error constants in `constants/`, types in `types/`, log errors via centralized logger, and maintain >= 90% unit test coverage.
- Audit all database queries for efficiency and log warnings for slow queries (>100ms). Minimize database compute hours with TTL query caching, projection selection, and Prisma indexes. Integrate GraphQL (`/api/graphql`) for single round-trip data fetching. Keep GraphQL SDL/queries in `constants/` and types in `types/`. Maintain >= 90% unit test coverage.
- Protect all sensitive data at rest and in transit using authenticated AES-256-GCM. Generate cryptographically secure 12-byte IVs per operation and strictly verify 16-byte authentication tags on decryption. Sourced keys must be 256 bits (32 bytes) from environment or PBKDF2/SHA-256 derivation. Keep crypto constants in `constants/crypto.ts` and types in `types/crypto.ts`. Never log plaintext keys. Maintain >= 90% unit test coverage individually.
- Automatically identify, audit, upgrade, and maintain all core tech stack components, runtime environments, framework dependencies, and third-party libraries to latest LTS or stable versions. Systematically refactor breaking changes, deprecation notices, and updated library APIs across the codebase. Validate every upgrade through the complete quality check pipeline (build execution, typechecking, linting, and running unit tests with >= 90% per-file coverage) to prevent regressions and maintain stability.
- Continuously audit, identify, and apply automated performance optimizations across the entire codebase. Proactively optimize critical paths, implement efficient code-splitting, lazy-loading (`next/dynamic`), and resource caching. Validate all performance improvements against established bundle size and latency benchmarks via the quality check pipeline. Maintain >= 90% unit test coverage on all performance helpers.
- Continuously monitor, analyze, and resolve application bugs and errors captured in log files (`logs/app.log`, `logs/error.log`). Automatically parse runtime log outputs, stack traces, and error codes to diagnose underlying issues, implement verified bug fixes, and prevent recurring failures. Validate all bug fixes through the quality check pipeline (linting, typechecking, test suites) with >= 90% per-file coverage, ensuring no regressions.
- Automatically identify, analyze, and resolve all compiler, linter, runtime, and dependency warnings across the entire project. Proactively apply safe refactoring and fixes for deprecation notices, unused imports, type mismatches, and syntax warnings without breaking core functionality. Validate all warning fixes by running the complete quality check pipeline (linting, typechecking, builds, and unit tests with >= 90% per-file coverage).
- Enforce git pre-commit hooks executing all quality checks (linting, typechecking, building, and running tests with >= 90% per-file coverage) before allowing any commit. Never bypass pre-commit hooks.
- Strictly prohibit direct DOM manipulation using low-level libraries or browser APIs (`document.getElementById`, `document.querySelector`, `document.createElement`, `element.appendChild`, `element.removeChild`, `element.innerHTML`, manual `classList.add/remove`, or jQuery) within the application framework. All UI updates, styling, conditional renders, and file downloads must be handled through declarative framework state management patterns (React state, hooks, context) so the framework view engine remains the single source of truth. Validate all declarative refactors with >= 90% per-file unit test coverage.
- Enforce strict client-side performance budgets across build tools and CI/CD pipelines (maximum 250 KB gzip for shared client JavaScript and 50 KB gzip for critical CSS). Integrate the automated check command (`npm run check:budget`) into build, pre-commit, and pull request quality gates to fail immediately on budget exceedance. Code-split heavy libraries (such as `xlsx`) on demand. Maintain >= 90% unit test coverage individually on all performance budget modules.
- Ensure that after every change the system executes the appropriate quality check commands where AI coding agents will check for build issues, typecheck issues, lint issues, unit test code coverage (>= 90% per-file), apply pending database schema migrations, and evaluate performance budgets. Build and unit test code coverage MUST be evaluated first (`npm run build && npm run test:coverage && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run db:push && npm run check:budget`). In multi-project workspaces, use global commands in root package.json (`npm run quality` or `npm run check:all`). Use fast differential checks for rapid iteration on changed files (`npm run quality:fast` or `npm run check:fast`).
- Enforce the strictest linter configuration across all monorepo packages (backend and frontend): zero `any` (`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`), explicit return types for functions/methods (`@typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type`), disallow non-null assertions `!` (`@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion`), enforce type-only imports (`import type`), enforce optional chaining (`?.`), zero unused variables/imports (`@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` with `^_` pattern), and strict naming conventions (PascalCase for types, camelCase for variables/functions). In React/Next.js, enforce hook rules, disallow unsafe rendering (`react/no-danger`), require clean boolean attributes, and enforce accessibility (`jsx-a11y/alt-text`, `jsx-a11y/no-redundant-roles`, `jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid`). Ensure max cyclomatic complexity 10, max file lines 300, max line length 120, single quotes, semicolons, no trailing commas, prefer-const, no-var, and object-shorthand. Guarantee zero ESLint errors and zero ESLint warnings across the entire repository. Linting is integrated into the primary build command (`npm run build`), pre-commit hooks (`npm run pre-commit`), and PR CI/CD workflows (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Maintain >= 90% unit test coverage individually across all refactored files and helpers.
